assessments.reasoning: The visually checked December 1, 1976 Xerox cover describes the initial Alto Mesa programming-system release, and the dated preface says individual sections bear their own release dates. Jim Mitchell’s November 2, 1976 addendum identifies the manual’s subject as the Mesa language expected at the first-quarter 1977 compiler transfer. It distinguishes the then-current language from the version presented in the manual and identifies the included grammar as a reference for the then-current language. Addendum section A.2 corroborates the grammar’s inclusion and location.

challenge.method: Reacquire the exact registered scan, visually inspect the dated cover and preface and the signed addendum and grammar, recompute page and excerpt hashes, and test the alternatives of compiler description, completed transfer, target-language grammar, and a single date for every collected component.
challenge.results: The manual presents the expected Mesa language. Compiler transfer gives the planned timing. The addendum identifies the grammar as current at its own date. The preface and the separately March 1, 1976 binding-facilities heading show that the collection includes individually dated components. Those controls support the revised limited attribution.

limitations: The dated collection describes the initial Alto system release. Its cover date does not independently date the release or all collected components.
The signed addendum records prospective timing and a documentary comparison. Actual transfer, delivery, compiler contents, and compatibility require separate evidence.
The literal cover date was verified visually because its OCR line misreads the printed numeral. The checked OCR ranges are location witnesses rather than authoritative transcriptions.
